sub_answers.sub_question: What disputes arose over representation of Bosnia's ethnic groups within the national team and football association?
sub_answers.text: Football was divided along ethnic lines during and after the Bosnian War, producing disputes over representation between Bosniaks, Croats and Serbs in national structures and teams [d55965203s4p0][d18600876s11p0]. In 1993 Bosnian Croats launched the Football Federation of Herzeg-Bosnia and a Croat-only First League of Herzeg-Bosnia [d55965203s4p0]. In the same year Bosnian Serbs organised the First League of the Republika Srpska on territory controlled by the Republika Srpska regime [d55965203s4p0]. Competition under the Bosnian FA (N/FSBiH) came largely to a standstill and its competitions reflected a Bosniak majority in that period [d55965203s4p0].

sub_answers.text: A hastily arranged Bosnia-Herzegovina humanitarian team played two friendlies in March 1993 as an initial step toward forming a national side [d8582465s6p0]. The Bosnia and Herzegovina national team began playing official matches in late November 1995 [d8582465s6p0].

sub_answers.text: The Bosnian Football Association (N/FSBiH) applied for FIFA and UEFA membership after independence in late winter 1992 [d55965203s4p0]. In 1993 Bosnian Croats formed the Football Federation of Herzeg-Bosnia and launched the First League of Herzeg-Bosnia for Croat clubs [d55965203s4p0]. In 1993 Bosnian Serbs organized the First League of the Republika Srpska on territory they controlled [d55965203s4p0]. Competition under N/FSBiH auspices resumed with the official launch of the Bosnian First League in the 1995–96 season [d55965203s4p0]. The Bosnia and Herzegovina national team progressed from 1993 humanitarian friendlies to playing official matches beginning in late November 1995 [d8582465s6p0].

Which controversies have occurred over how Bosniak, Croat and Serb communities are represented in the Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team roster, coaching staff, and the composition of the Football Association (N/FSBiH)?
sub_answers.text: Football in Bosnia and Herzegovina split along ethnic lines during the war, with Bosnian Croats forming the Football Federation of Herzeg-Bosnia and Bosnian Serbs organizing the First League of the Republika Srpska, producing separate competitions and de facto separate representation [d55965203s4p0]. The N/FSBiH retained oversight only in territory under Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina institutions and had a Bosniak majority during the conflict period described [d55965203s4p0]. The ethno-national contest over Bosnia's identity and institutions is documented as a broader source of confrontation affecting Bosniak, Croat and Serb relations, which contextualises disputes over representation in national institutions including sport [d18600876s11p0].
